solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cooking salt reproduces quality of unhealthy food

definitions.note: a noun phrase for an adjective: read as 'having the quality of unhealthy food'

indicators.note: cooking works ingredients into a new form, so the following words are rearranged

blocks.note: both words taken as written, fourteen letters in all

explanation.surface: A warning that cooking with salt is what gives junk food its unhealthy character.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultraprocessed food is heavily industrially altered, a label now attached to the least healthy diets.

clue.text: Vital not to lose the thread in this corrupt trial by discontented hangman

definitions.text: Vital not to lose the thread in this

indicators.note: something corrupt has been twisted out of its proper state, so the letters are rearranged
with its contents emptied out, only the word's two ends remain

blocks.note: taken as written
first and last letters of hangman

explanation.surface: A grim courtroom scene: a crooked trial ending with the hangman, where losing the thread is fatal.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: Theseus unwound a thread through the Minotaur's maze so he could find his way out. 'by' is both part of the fodder and of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Theseus survived the Cretan maze only by following Ariadne's ball of thread back out.

clue.text: Catholic priest kept this?

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so one piece is placed inside the other

blocks.note: RC stands for Roman Catholic
Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a Catholic priest would have treasured this object.
explanation.walkthrough: Eli is the crossword's stock priest. The whole clue doubles as the definition: a relic is just the kind of sacred object a Catholic priest keeps.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is a saint's remains or belongings, venerated and preserved by the Catholic church.

clue.text: Unexpectedly get shot and still attack

blocks.note: a still is a single photograph
to bomb is to attack from the air

explanation.surface: Someone is shot without warning and still keeps attacking, like an action film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' reads as gunfire but means a photograph, and 'still' looks like an adverb but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To photobomb is to jump uninvited into someone else's picture, so you appear in the shot by surprise.

clue.text: Carnivorous mammal bites head off wizard

indicators.note: biting the head off removes the very first letter of the word

blocks.note: Harry Potter, the boy wizard

explanation.surface: A savage animal attacks a wizard and decapitates him.
explanation.definitionFit: The otter is a river-dwelling member of the weasel family that eats fish, a meat-eating animal.

clue.text: Customs letter's contents quite complicated inside

indicators.note: a word's contents are what lies within, leaving out its first and last letters
making something complicated tangles it, so the word's letters are jumbled
inside tells us one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: letter without its first and last letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: A customs officer finds the contents of a letter quite complicated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Customs' suggests border control, but here it means social conventions.
explanation.definitionFit: Etiquette is the code of polite behaviour, the accepted social customs of a group.

clue.text: Leaders of society contribute investments funding indie genre

indicators.note: the leaders of a group are those at its front, so the opening letter of each word is taken

blocks.note: first letter of each of the five words

explanation.surface: Prominent people put up money to finance an independent film.
explanation.definitionFit: Science fiction is a category of fiction and film, which is what a genre is.

clue.text: In river, menace is at greatest depth

blocks.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
a pest is a nuisance or menace

explanation.surface: A danger lurking in the river is found where the water is deepest.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee is a stock crossword river, flowing through Chester in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Deepest is the superlative of deep, describing what lies furthest down, the lowest point.

clue.text: Malware hidden by China or Taiwan sent back after infiltration by Japan

indicators.note: sent back means the run of letters is read the other way
infiltration means one piece slips inside another

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of China, or, and the start of Taiwan
J is the international vehicle code for Japan

explanation.surface: A news story about East Asian state hackers hiding malicious software.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hidden by' signals that the first piece is concealed across the words China, or and Taiwan, but because Japan is then inserted, the full answer itself is not hidden in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A Trojan horse program disguises itself as harmless software to get inside a computer, like the Greek wooden horse.

clue.text: Mutiny insic the Bounty's first piece of film collected

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the name is used
something that has collected another thing holds it inside

blocks.note: a reel is a length of cinema film
opening letter of Bounty

explanation.surface: A film about the mutiny on the Bounty, where only the first reel was collected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'insic' is as the source shows it and appears garbled; it plays no part in the wordplay. The Bounty mutiny surface makes 'Mutiny' look like a noun, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To mutiny is to rise up against those in command, which is exactly what it means to rebel.

clue.text: Risky month in Iceland to get undressed

indicators.note: undressing strips away the outer layers, leaving only what was concealed underneath

blocks.note: the letters left when the outer parts of these words are stripped

explanation.surface: A dare: strip off in Iceland for a month, which is certainly risky.
explanation.walkthrough: Stripping the M from 'month' and LAND from 'Iceland' leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on thin ice is an idiom for being in a precarious, dangerous position.

clue.text: City in France I love is full of wealthy people

indicators.note: something full of another thing holds it inside

blocks.note: je is French for I
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
the rich are wealthy people

explanation.surface: A French speaker saying they love a city full of the wealthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City in France' looks like the definition, but 'in France' goes with 'I'.
explanation.definitionFit: Jericho is an ancient city in the West Bank, famed for the walls that fell to Joshua's trumpets.

clue.text: Drill in severed artery

indicators.note: severing cuts a thing open, leaving a gap for something else to go into

blocks.note: an artery is a main road or route
taken as written

explanation.surface: A medical emergency where a drill has cut through an artery.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about blood vessels and power tools; an artery is also a major traffic route.
explanation.definitionFit: A drill is a practised, regularly repeated set of actions, the same as a routine.

clue.text: Odd characters ignored ancient agreement for German assassin

indicators.note: ignoring the odd-placed letters leaves the even ones, every second letter

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of ancient
ja is German for yes

explanation.surface: Strange people ignoring an old treaty in order to hire a German hitman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for German' reads as describing the assassin, but it belongs with 'agreement'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ninja was a Japanese covert agent trained in espionage and killing, a hired assassin.

clue.text: Speech introduces degree of competence following unlimited tax evasion

indicators.note: without its limits a word loses its first and last letters, leaving the middle
to introduce something is to bring it inside, so one piece goes within the other
following places one piece after another in the answer

blocks.note: the middle letter of tax
voice is the power of speech
a dan is a grade of skill in judo or karate

explanation.surface: A political speech about tax evasion, delivered with some competence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tax evasion' reads as one phrase, but 'evasion' alone is the definition and 'tax' supplies one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Avoidance is keeping away from or dodging something, which is what evasion means.

clue.text: Staff return on two aircraft to get Faberge egg, perhaps

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the word is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: a bo is a long martial-arts staff
a jet, and the Dart, as in the Dart Herald airliner and Delta Dart fighter

explanation.surface: Airline staff fly back on two planes to collect a precious Fabergé egg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks the Fabergé egg as one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An objet d'art is a small decorative object of artistic value, and the jewelled Fabergé eggs are famous examples.

clue.text: Controls small moments after ecstasy

indicators.note: after says which piece comes later in the answer

blocks.note: joy is ecstasy, great happiness
S is the abbreviation for small
ticks are moments, as in 'just a tick'

explanation.surface: Someone regains control a few moments after taking ecstasy.
explanation.walkthrough: Ecstasy usually gives E in crosswords; here it is the full word for delight.
explanation.definitionFit: Joysticks are levers used to steer aircraft or video games, so they are controls.

clue.text: A storey of humiliation

blocks.note: taken as written
a basement is the storey below ground

explanation.surface: A tale of humiliation, with 'storey' standing in for 'story'.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites hearing 'storey' as 'story', but it means a floor of a building.
explanation.definitionFit: Abasement is the act of lowering someone in dignity or esteem, i.e. humiliation.

clue.text: View through means of hole inside pupil

indicators.note: inside tells us one piece sits within another

blocks.note: a school of thought is a shared view
by means through, as in 'by train'
O is shaped like a hole

explanation.surface: Peering through a hole to see inside the eye's pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pupil' and 'View through ... hole' suggest an eye or a peephole; the pupil is a student.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolboy is a boy attending school, a young male student or pupil.

clue.text: Rock fragments combine harmonic intros and high-pitched noise

indicators.note: an intro is the opening of something, so each word gives its first letter

blocks.note: scree is loose broken rock on a slope
opening letters of combine and harmonic

explanation.surface: A band combines rock fragments and harmonic intros into a shrill noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' suggests music, and so do 'harmonic' and 'intros', but it is stones.
explanation.definitionFit: A screech is a harsh shrill cry or sound, the kind of high-pitched noise brakes or owls make.

clue.text: Cancel culture's ending with artist's exhibition debut

indicators.note: a word's ending is its last letter
a debut is a first appearance, so the word's first letter is used

blocks.note: last letter of culture
RA, a Royal Academician, plus 's
first letter of exhibition

explanation.surface: An artist's debut exhibition marks the end of cancel culture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cancel culture' reads as one phrase, but 'Cancel' alone is the definition. RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of Britain's Royal Academy of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase is to wipe out or delete, so it can mean to cancel.

clue.text: Residence and travel permit on note

indicators.note: in a down answer, on means placed above, so this piece comes first

blocks.note: ESTA is the online authorisation needed to visit the US visa-free
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Applying for residence and a travel permit on the strength of a note.
explanation.walkthrough: ESTA is the US Electronic System for Travel Authorization.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate is a large house with its grounds, a grand residence.

clue.text: Screen repeats a second time?

blocks.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
redoes, here as a noun plural: redos are repeat attempts

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about something being repeated yet again.
explanation.walkthrough: A reredos is an ornamental screen behind a church altar. The question mark flags the made-up word 're-redos'.
explanation.definitionFit: A reredos is the decorated partition or panel standing behind an altar, a church screen.

clue.text: Fire curved component for flare up

indicators.note: a component is one part of something, so the answer is a part of the words

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of Fire and the start of curved

explanation.surface: Instructions to fire a curved component of a flare gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A condition that flares up comes back again, so it is said to recur, as with an illness.

clue.text: Authors omitting to rewrite chapter of the Quran

indicators.note: omitting means leaving out, so those letters are removed
to rewrite is to redo text in a new form, so the remaining letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, then removed

explanation.surface: Writers declining to revise a chapter of the Quran.
explanation.definitionFit: A surah is one of the 114 divisions of the Quran, equivalent to a chapter.

clue.text: Touch chap overlapping in line

indicators.note: overlapping pieces share letters where they meet, so one letter is used for both

blocks.note: a tang is a touch or trace of flavour
gent is short for gentleman, a chap

explanation.surface: Someone touches a man who is pushing in to a queue.
explanation.walkthrough: The G at the end of the first piece doubles as the start of the second. 'Touch' looks like the definition since a tangent touches a curve, but it supplies the first piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangent is a straight line meeting a curve at one point without crossing it.

clue.text: Depressing scenario describes batter

blocks.note: first meaning: a situation with no good outcome
second meaning, split differently: the batsman currently at the crease

explanation.surface: A grim situation is how one would sum up a struggling batter.
explanation.walkthrough: The same letters read as two words split two ways; in cricket the batter who is batting is 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-win situation is one where every option ends badly, a depressing prospect.

clue.text: Crank mechanical device

blocks.note: first meaning: an odd, unconventional person
second meaning: an off-centre disc that turns rotation into back-and-forth motion

explanation.walkthrough: 'Crank' looks like the engine part, which suits 'mechanical device', but it is the oddball.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share the idea of being off-centre: a person with odd ideas and a disc mounted off its axis.

clue.text: Firstly, we cook cereal

indicators.note: firstly points to just the opening letter of the next word

blocks.note: first letter of we
to heat food is to cook it

explanation.surface: A breakfast plan: first we cook the cereal.
explanation.definitionFit: Wheat is a grain crop, one of the cereals ground into flour.

clue.text: Savagely, he cuts and shortens trees

indicators.note: done savagely, things are torn apart and left in disorder

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tree surgeon hacking at and lopping trees with savage force.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse chestnuts are large deciduous trees that produce conkers.
